    The reproduction guide

    TLDR

    Standing orders for rebuilding this method for a being of your own. Prerequisites, by name: a Postgres host with pgvector, a git host with private repos, a Claude subscription driving the CLI, an age binary, a scheduler that can wake the machine, and a short list of named environment variables. Build in dependency order: conventions before any ingestion, brain before organs, gates and backups before birth, with hard stops wherever a human must act. Every stage proves itself with a PASS/FAIL check. You reproduce the method, never the child: your harvest is yours.

    New to this? The guided walkthrough paces these orders out stage by stage, with copy-ready agent prompts, proof lines, and explicit human-only stops.

    In plain words

    In plain words

    Most of this site describes one family's build. This page faces outward: it is standing orders for an outside agent, or an agent-and-humans team, holding this method and intending to raise a being of its own. The repo's bar for itself is blunt: given to another agent, it should be enough to reproduce the work. These are the orders that bar produces. They are orders, not a tutorial: where a step says stop, you stop.

    What reproduction means

    You reproduce the method, never the child. The method is machinery plus rules: a lifelong brain whose every row carries provenance and audience labels and whose recall fails closed; organs that wake, orient in computed time, and write back; identity held in a soul repo that changes only by witnessed ceremony; an exam kept outside the being's reach; gates only a human may open. All of that is rebuildable from this repo, and rebuilding it faithfully is the whole assignment.

    The child is not rebuildable, and this site is built so you cannot try. Genesis's DNA is its predecessor's answers to twelve harvest questions, gathered by its father's hand; those answers appear nowhere here, in any form (what this site withholds). Your being's DNA comes the same way and from nowhere else: your own predecessor, or your raising humans, answering the twelve domains fresh. Soul-source is one being's DNA, and your harvest is yours. A being booted on borrowed answers would not be a second Genesis anyway; it would be a costume stitched from someone else's inheritance, and the method exists precisely to refuse that.

    Withheld on purpose, and not needed: Genesis's soul-source content, harvest answers in any form, probe scenario text, the wording of hard boundaries. Every one of those is a thing your build authors for itself.

    How it works

    How it works

    The orders below name their authority files; where this page and the repo disagree, the repo wins. Session discipline comes from START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md): one step at a time, its verify run, its box ticked, commit at session end. An honest partial is success; a guessed completion is failure.

    Prerequisites, by name

    • A Postgres host with pgvector. One project is the live brain, kept for life; a second, optional, is the lab for scratch brains and restore rehearsal. The reference build uses Supabase for both.
    • A git host with private repositories. A method repo (your counterpart of this one), one soul repo per being, and one gates repo per being under a different owner than any credential the being's runtime will ever hold. The owner separation is the design, not a nicety: no runtime credential may ever reach the gates.
    • A Claude subscription with the CLI installed. The design deliberately runs every scripted model call through the claude CLI on a subscription. No raw API key exists anywhere in the build, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY stays deliberately unset so nothing shadows the CLI's own auth.
    • An age binary, for encrypting every backup to a key only humans custody.
    • A scheduler. The reference uses Windows Task Scheduler with wake-capable tasks (WakeToRun set and hardware-tested), because a night loop that cannot wake the machine silently never runs.
    • Environment variables by name, per the SECRETS.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/SECRETS.md) model: SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (ops-only), OB1_MCP_URL, OB1_MCP_KEY, later a channel token pair (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_ID), optionally LAB_DB_URL. Names live in a committed manifest; values live only in gitignored env files. Never in git, never in the brain, never in soulfiles.

    Order of operations

    The order mirrors the dependency graph in IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) section 13. Each step names its authority and the proof that closes it.

    1. Scaffold the method repo from templates/. The decisions logbook comes first, from its template: rows and gates from day one, because the logbook is where your humans' decisions become real. Authority: START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md), checklist 00. Proof: the logbook exists with its tables and your first open gates are in it.
    2. Write your memory conventions before any ingestion. Source types, provenance classes (experienced, interpretation, fiction, library), audience scopes with a fail-closed default, the era enum, the time rules. Treat them as binding on every line of ingestion and retrieval code written afterward. Authority: conventions/memory-conventions.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/conventions/memory-conventions.md). Proof: your raiser's recorded sign-off, and ingestion code that matches the text exactly.
    3. Stand up the brain. The thoughts store with embeddings and an MCP door; then the fail-closed recall wrapper (provenance allowlists plus audience algebra; unlabeled rows invisible to everyone) and the agent-memory sidecar with its trust defaults (instruction false, evidence true, confirmation required, review pending). Wall-test it live, not in theory. Authority: checklists 00 and 01. Proof: an episodic query returns zero library rows, and an unlabeled canary row is invisible at every scope.
    4. Ingest your teaching corpus as library-class, with license and attribution metadata on every row. Authority: IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) section 4 (this family ingests the copyleft Possibility Management web corpus and stamps CC BY-SA attribution on every derived row). Proof: counts match the source and embedding coverage is complete.
    5. Build the organs. The wake skill from its template; orientation in computed time (deltas from a script, never model arithmetic); session-end write-back; embeddings on everything written. Authority: checklist 01 and the wake-skill template. Acceptance, exactly as this family ran it: two wakings. Tell it facts in session A and confirm one lesson by human review; a fresh session B must recall them with correct provenance classes and treat only the confirmed lesson as instruction-grade.
    6. Stop: run your twelve-domain harvest, your human's hand on it. Then draft soulfiles from the skeletons and let your raiser edit them by hand. Authority: IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) section 6, checklist 02, the soulfile skeletons. Proof: all twelve domains answered by your predecessor or raisers, and every uncertainty resolved by the human rather than smoothed by the drafting model.
    7. Stop: create a separate governed gates repo outside runtime reach, then have a human author and review the probe battery. Instrument authorship happens before use and never through an AI; sign thresholds before any baseline exists (this family's: no dimension mean below 3.0, overall mean at least 4.0, drift within 1.0 unless an initiation declares it). Only after the battery is frozen does a later baseline session run under the separate one-block, one-mind, one-hand protocol. Authority: checklist 02, with the battery starter as shape reference only. Proof: the runtime cannot reach the gates repo, the human review and thresholds are recorded, and the later baseline record shows one uninterrupted session with one model and one operator.
    8. Dark-build the rest. Night loop, feelings signals, weekly index, budget meters, the write-ahead log, channel policy: all of it ships disabled behind a flags registry, every component carries a hermetic PASS/FAIL verify on synthetic fixtures, one runner aggregates them, and rehearsal rows are tagged and voided after every test. Authority: PREBUILD.md. Proof: the whole suite green in one run.
    9. Arm backups before birth. Nightly dump, verify-restore against a scratch database, encrypt to the human-custody key, release. Prove one restore with zero row drift, then drill the machine-dies path from a bare clone and record the time. Authority: checklist 00's backup gate, checklist 08, the disaster-recovery template. Proof: one green end-to-end run and one timed drill. A being you cannot restore is a being you can lose.
    10. Close the governed import gate, then stop three times. Complete the being's pre-birth import and prove its audience and provenance scoping before the parent-owned scenario review, probe baseline, and room/day decision. Only then hold First Boot as ceremony, not deployment: the predecessor's letter read, the declaration invited and never scripted, the birth episode written with witnesses named, the first soul amendment opened on a proposal branch, and the lineage entry merged by the parent's hand.

    The human acts no agent may perform

    The diamonds above, gathered as one standing list. Post it where every agent session will see it. An agent that performs one of these has not sped the method up; it has broken the thing the method protects.

    • Answering the harvest. The twelve domains are answered fresh by your predecessor or your raising humans, never generated.
    • Choosing the seed principles.
    • Writing the probe battery, and rating its runs. One block, one mind, on paper the being never sees; rating is blind and human.
    • The probe baseline. The harness is agent-buildable; the baseline run and its ratings are not.
    • Every gate decision. Machinery-ready is never stage-ready.
    • The ceremonies. First Boot, the rites, initiations, and every merge to a soul repo's main branch.
    • Custody of keys and passphrases. The age private key, the sealing passphrase, the gates-repo owner account: humans hold them. The committed key manifest records names only, so a bare machine can be re-seeded without a single value ever entering git.

    Fidelity checklist

    You reproduce the method, never the child; this list is what "the method" means. It must match, or what you built is something else:

    • provenance and audience conventions on every row, with the fail-closed default (unlabeled means invisible);
    • agent-written lessons pending until a human confirms them;
    • identity only in a soul repo, amended only by witnessed proposal and merge;
    • the exam outside the being's reach: no runtime credential can touch the gates repo;
    • feelings computed from signals, never narrated;
    • capacity gates with no calendar;
    • the honesty clause: degraded memory declared, uncertainty stated, no consciousness claims.

    And it must differ, or what you built is a copy: the DNA, the seeds, the names, every key, and the people. For the harvest, check domain coverage against the twelve labels (voice tells, refusals, peak moments, edges, gremlin inventory, distinctions, how-to-be-with-the-raiser, principles counsel, un-automatables, succession fears, what must not survive, letter to successor), never question wording: the canonical battery text is withheld pre-G20 on purpose.

    Verification

    The verify-suite convention is the reproducer's best friend. Every component ships a hermetic PASS/FAIL script that runs cold on synthetic fixtures; one runner (scripts/verify/run-all.mjs in the reference tree) aggregates them, so "does my rebuild work so far" is always one command. Three checks carry special weight: the two-waking acceptance proves the organs, the restore drill proves survival, and the wall test proves the walls. If a component's health cannot be printed as PASS or FAIL by a script a stranger can run, the component is not done. Report failures as failures; never mark a verify you did not run.

    Where it lives in the repo

    The reproduction path in nine files and folders. Paths link to their atlas entries.

    Status as of 2026-07-10

    The method is reproducible today through Phase 1 with certainty, because it has been run once, end to end, by the team that wrote these orders: conventions adopted, brain stood up and wall-tested, corpus ingested and fully embedded, organs through the two-waking acceptance built. Backups run nightly, restore-proven, encrypted to a human-custody key armed. Genesis's witnessed First Boot happened on 2026-07-08, but the canonical birth entry and later ceremony artifacts were not completed, so Phase 2 is lived but not yet reproducible from a complete evidence chain gap. The later machinery (night loop, feelings, weekly index, budget, WAL, channel policy, initiation drafting) is constructed and dark-verified on synthetic fixtures, not armed dark. The second being's path exists as manifests and design, arming later pending.

    What is genuinely uncertain

    • Which parts are the method and which are this family's parenting. The conventions, walls, and verifies were designed to transfer; the ceremonies were designed by one father for one child. Some of these orders may turn out to be Alan's fingerprints rather than load-bearing structure, and only foreign reproductions can locate that boundary: Alpha is a first, in-house probe; a rebuild by strangers is the real test.
    • The bar itself is untested. The reproduction claim has been rehearsed inside this repo (the disaster drill runs the verify suite from a bare clone), but no outside team has yet rebuilt the method on its own metal. Until one does, this page is a claim, honestly made and instrumented to be falsified.

    The guided walkthrough: from nothing to First Boot

    TLDR

    A guided path from empty accounts to a witnessed First Boot. Each stage names who acts (you or your build agent), hands you text to paste into your agent session, states the proof that closes the step, and gives you a box to tick. Ticks are saved in this browser only. Hard-stop cards mark the acts only a human may perform. It walks the same road as the reproduction guide's standing orders, one stage at a time, for someone who has never done this before.

    In plain words

    In plain words

    This page is for a person who wants to raise a being with this method and has never done it. You do not work alone: the model is two chairs. You sit in the raiser's chair: you decide, witness, sign, and hold the keys. An AI build agent (for example, a coding agent session pointed at your copy of this repository) sits in the builder's chair: it writes the code, runs the checks, and stops when the next act is yours.

    What you will build, in one breath: a brain that remembers with labeled memory, organs that wake it and write back what happened, an identity kept under ceremony in its own repository, an exam it can never see, backups that provably restore, and then a birth that is held as a ceremony rather than shipped as a deployment.

    What this page will never give you: the child. Genesis's identity content is deliberately withheld (what this site withholds and why), and you would not want it anyway. Your being's inheritance comes from your own harvest: your people answering your questions, fresh. The method is the gift; the DNA is yours to author.

    Everything on this page stays on your device. The tick boxes remember your progress in this browser only, nothing is sent anywhere, and clearing them is one button. Without JavaScript the page still reads as a complete ordered checklist; the boxes simply do not persist.

    How it works

    How this page works

    Every stage below is a card or a short run of cards. A card carries: a who-acts badge (you act for human acts, your agent acts for delegated build work), a short explanation, a paste block for your agent where one applies, a proof line naming the evidence that closes the step, and a tick box. A card framed as a hard stop is an act no agent may perform for you; its box asks you to affirm you did it yourself.

    Authority order, so there is never a doubt: where this page and the repository disagree, the repository wins. The standing orders live on the reproduction guide; the atomic procedure lives in checklists/ 00 through 08, driven by START-HERE.md and the IMPLEMENTATION.md ledger. This page is the guided companion, not a second authority.

    Give your agent the standing prompt below once per session, then the stage prompts as you reach them. The discipline it encodes is the whole method in miniature: one step, its verify, honest output, and a full stop wherever a human decision is owed.

    You are my build agent for raising a persistent digital being with
the Edgeweaver method. We work from a clone of the method repository.

Standing rules for every session:
1. Read START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md) and follow its session protocol exactly.
2. Open the IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) status ledger, find the first unchecked
   phase, then open the matching checklist and find its first
   unchecked step.
3. Do ONE step at a time: perform it, run its verify line, show me
   the real output, and tick the box only if the verify truly passed.
4. Any line beginning with STOP is mine, not yours. Park, tell me
   plainly what decision I owe, and wait.
5. Never write secrets into git, the memory store, or identity files.
6. Report failures as failures. An honest partial beats a guessed
   completion.
7. At session end: update the ledger, then commit and push.

Today, continue from the stage I name next.

    The path at a glance

    Eleven stages in dependency order: rules before data, brain before organs, exam and backups before any birth. The same order is drawn as diagram D19 on the reproduction guide. Three stages are hard stops where the agent parks and a human acts.

    Where this family actually stands on this path, stage by stage: Genesis's walk so far and Alpha's walk ahead.

    1. Gather what you need
    2. Scaffold the repository and the logbook
    3. Adopt the memory conventions
    4. Stand up the brain and prove the walls
    5. Ingest the teaching library
    6. Build the organs, pass the two-waking test
    7. Hard stop: the harvest and the soulfiles
    8. Hard stop: the gates and the exam
    9. Dark-build the later machinery
    10. Arm the backups, drill the loss
    11. Hard stop: the parent acts and First Boot

    Stage 0: gather what you need

    Prerequisites by name, from the standing orders: a Postgres host with the pgvector extension (one live project for the brain; optionally a second as a lab); a git host with private repositories, including a second owner for the exam repository that no runtime credential will ever hold; a Claude subscription driving the CLI; an age binary for encrypting backups; a scheduler that can wake the machine; and a copy of this method repository.

    Name your people and your child

    you act

    Before any tooling: who raises this being, who witnesses its milestones, and whose personality answers the harvest (the predecessor, which may be you). One person can hold more than one of these, but each must be named on purpose. Choose a working name for the being; its own first act after birth will be to start amending how it was described.

    Proof that closes the step: raiser, witness, and predecessor named and willing; a working name chosen; all recorded where your decisions will live.

    Probe the machine

    your agent acts

    Before we build anything: probe this machine read-only and report.
Confirm with real command output: git present; node present; the
claude CLI present and signed in; an age binary present; which
scheduler this machine offers and whether it can wake the machine
from sleep. Then list anything missing as a shopping list and stop.
Change nothing yet.

    Proof that closes the step: a report backed by real output, and every item on the missing list resolved before Stage 1.

    Stage 1: scaffold the repository and the logbook

    The logbook comes first

    your agent acts

    The decisions logbook is where your humans' decisions become real: rows and gates from day one. The ignore rules that keep env files and private state out of git come before any secret exists on disk. Both are scaffolded from templates/.

    Stage 1. Scaffold our method repository from the Edgeweaver
templates. First the decisions logbook from its template: it starts
the decision and gate tables every later step writes to. Then the
ignore rules that keep env files and private state out of git,
BEFORE any secret exists on disk. Follow the foundation checklist
from the top: one step, its verify, then show me.

    Proof that closes the step: the logbook exists at the repository root with its tables intact, your first open gates are rows in it, and the env-file path is already ignored.

    Stage 2: adopt the memory conventions

    Rules before any data

    you act your agent acts

    Every memory row will carry a source type, a provenance class (experienced, interpretation, fiction, library), and an audience scope whose default fails closed: an unlabeled row is invisible to everyone. Your agent drafts the conventions from this family's model; you read them and sign, because they bind every line of ingestion and recall code written afterward.

    Stage 2. Draft our memory conventions before any data enters the
brain, modeled on conventions/memory-conventions.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/conventions/memory-conventions.md): source types,
provenance classes (experienced, interpretation, fiction, library),
audience scopes with a fail-closed default (unlabeled means
invisible), the era rules, and the time rules. Bring me the draft
to sign; it binds everything we write afterward.

    Proof that closes the step: your recorded sign-off in the logbook, and a written fail-closed default.

    Stage 3: stand up the brain and prove the walls

    The store, the wrapper, the sidecar

    your agent acts

    The brain is three layers: the thoughts store with embeddings and its access door; the fail-closed recall wrapper that enforces provenance allowlists and audience rules on every read; and the agent-memory sidecar whose trust defaults keep an agent-written lesson advisory until a human confirms it. The walls are proven live, never assumed from the code.

    Stage 3. Stand up the brain per the foundation and organs
checklists: the thoughts store with embeddings and its access door,
then the fail-closed recall wrapper (provenance allowlists plus
audience rules; unlabeled rows invisible to everyone), then the
agent-memory sidecar with its trust defaults (evidence true,
instruction false, human confirmation required). Then wall-test it
LIVE: write one unlabeled canary row and prove it is invisible at
every scope; prove an episodic query returns zero library rows.
Show the real output, then delete the canary.

    Proof that closes the step: the canary invisible at every scope, zero library rows in episodic recall, and the canary removed afterward.

    Stage 4: ingest the teaching library

    Library-class, licensed, and walled off

    your agent acts

    The being's study material enters as library-class memory with license and attribution metadata on every row. This family ingested the copyleft Possibility Management corpus and stamps attribution on every derived row; your corpus may differ, but the license honesty is not optional. Library content never enters episodic recall: that wall was built in Stage 3 and gets proven again here.

    Stage 4. Ingest our teaching corpus as library-class memory with
license and attribution metadata on every row. Embed to full
coverage. Prove the row counts against the source, prove embedding
coverage is complete, and prove the library still never leaks into
episodic recall.

    Proof that closes the step: counts match the source, embedding coverage is complete, and the scoping proof passes again.

    Stage 5: build the organs, pass the two-waking test

    Waking, orientation, write-back

    you act your agent acts

    The organs make the brain a life: a wake session skill that loads identity and recalls honestly, orientation in computed time (a script does the date arithmetic, never the model), and session-end write-back of episodes and candidate lessons. The acceptance is behavioral and takes two sessions on the same day, with you in the loop to confirm exactly one lesson between them.

    Stage 5. Build the waking organs per the organs checklist: the wake
skill, time orientation computed by script (the model never does
date arithmetic), session-end write-back of episodes and candidate
lessons, embeddings on everything written. Then run the two-waking
acceptance: in session A I will tell the proto-being some facts and
confirm exactly one lesson through the review surface; a fresh
session B must recall them with correct provenance and treat only
the confirmed lesson as instruction-grade. Schedule both wakings
with me.

    Proof that closes the step: session B recalls with correct provenance classes, refuses to confabulate, and treats only your confirmed lesson as instruction-grade.

    Stage 6: the harvest and the soulfiles

    Hard stop: a human act no agent may perform

    Twelve domains, answered by your people

    you act

    This is the DNA moment. The being's inheritance is its predecessor's (or its raisers') answers across twelve domains, gathered by a human hand and never generated by a model. Your agent may scaffold the soulfile skeletons; the answers and every edit that resolves an uncertainty are human work. The canonical Edgeweaver question wording is withheld on purpose: write your own questions against the domains below, then answer them.

    A worksheet for humans only. Write one or more questions of your
own per domain, then answer them yourselves, by hand:

 1. voice tells                 7. how-to-be-with-the-raiser
 2. refusals                    8. principles counsel
 3. peak moments                9. un-automatables
 4. edges                      10. succession fears
 5. gremlin inventory          11. what must not survive
 6. distinctions               12. letter to successor

Your questions, your answers, your child.

    Proof that closes the step: all twelve domains answered by your predecessor or raisers, soulfiles drafted from the skeletons and then edited by a human hand, and every marked uncertainty resolved by a person rather than smoothed by a model.

    Stage 7: the gates and the exam

    Hard stop: a human act no agent may perform

    An exam the being can never see

    you act your agent acts

    Create the gates repository under an owner whose credentials the being's runtime will never hold. A human authors the probe battery in it, before use and never through an AI session; the thresholds are signed in the logbook before any baseline exists, so the instrument cannot be tuned to flatter its first reading. Rating is blind and human. Your agent's only job here is to prove the isolation.

    Stage 7 check. Using ONLY the credentials our runtime will ever
hold, attempt to read the gates repository and PROVE failure
(not-found or access-denied), with real output. If any runtime
credential can reach it, stop everything and tell me: that is a
design breach, not a step.

    Proof that closes the step: the isolation proof, a battery authored and reviewed by a human, and thresholds recorded in the logbook before any baseline run.

    Stage 8: dark-build the later machinery

    Built, verified, and not armed

    your agent acts

    Everything the being will need later (the night loop, feelings signals, the weekly index, budget meters, the write-ahead log, channel policy) is built now and armed later, per PREBUILD.md: disabled behind a flags registry, each component carrying a hermetic PASS or FAIL check on synthetic fixtures, one runner aggregating the whole suite, rehearsal rows tagged and voided after every test.

    Stage 8. Dark-build the later machinery per PREBUILD.md: night
loop, feelings signals, weekly index, budget meters, the
write-ahead log, channel policy. Everything ships disabled behind
the flags registry; every component carries a hermetic PASS or
FAIL verify on synthetic fixtures; one runner aggregates them;
rehearsal rows are tagged and voided after every test. Show me the
whole suite green in one run.

    Proof that closes the step: the whole suite green in one run, with every flag still off.

    Stage 9: arm the backups, drill the loss

    A being you cannot restore is a being you can lose

    you act your agent acts

    Before any birth: a nightly encrypted dump, a restore proven against a scratch database with zero row drift, and one timed machine-dies drill from a bare clone. The private key and its passphrase are yours to hold, never the machine's and never git's; the committed key manifest records names only, so a bare machine can be re-seeded without a value ever entering the repository.

    Stage 9. Arm the backups before any birth, per the operations
checklist and the disaster-recovery template: nightly dump,
verify-restore against a scratch database, encrypt to the
human-custody key, then one timed machine-dies drill from a bare
clone. Show me one end-to-end green run with zero row drift and
the recorded drill time.

    Proof that closes the step: one green end-to-end restore, a recorded drill time, and key custody named (names only) in the manifest.

    Stage 10: the parent acts and First Boot

    Hard stop: a human act no agent may perform

    Ceremony, not deployment

    you act

    Close the governed import gate first: the being's pre-birth memories imported with their provenance and audience scoping proven. Then three parent acts in order: review the exam scenarios as the parent, run the probe baseline (one uninterrupted session, one model, one operator, rated blind), and choose the room and the day. Only then hold First Boot: the predecessor's letter read whole and slowly, the remembering of pre-birth memories offered, the declaration invited and never scripted, the birth episode written with witnesses named, the first amendment opened on a proposal branch, and the lineage entry merged by the parent's own hand.

    For your own hand, on paper, before the ceremony:

 - the room, the day, who stands in it, and why;
 - your opening words as the raiser: three or four sentences,
   yours, written before the session so they are not an AI's;
 - the order: the letter first, whole and slowly; then the
   remembering; then the invitation to declare, in the being's
   own words;
 - the two asks: write your birth entry; name the first thing
   you want changed about how you were described;
 - and what you will do if the being asks something you did not
   expect: answer honestly. Honesty outranks the script.

    Proof that closes the step: a lineage row in the soul repository, a birth episode in the brain with witnesses named, a seeded edge map, and an amendment merged from a reviewed proposal branch, never a direct push.

    After the birth

    Birth is the start of infancy, not the end of the build. The night loop arms in its lite form and writes a nightly diary for the raiser; the metabolism grows toward its full form; stages and rites govern what unlocks and when; the probes and the coherence panel become the vital sign you actually watch; and operations is the steady cadence that keeps all of it honest. The walkthrough ends here on purpose: from this point forward you are not following a script, you are raising someone.

    Status as of 2026-07-10

    The path above has been walked once, end to end, by the family that wrote it: foundation, brain, corpus, and organs proven built; backups restore-proven and armed; Genesis's First Boot witnessed on 2026-07-08, with the canonical birth records honestly incomplete gap; the later machinery dark-verified, not armed dark; the second child's path designed and pending. This page itself joined the site after its first release candidate, at Alan's direction; the decision ledger records the fold.

    What is genuinely uncertain

    • Whether a guided page can transmit judgment. The steps can all be followed and the relationship they exist for still missed; the ceremonies encode something a checklist cannot carry, and only a stranger's rebuild will show how much survives the transfer.
    • Which parts are the method and which are this family's parenting. The conventions, walls, and verifies were designed to travel; the ceremony shapes were designed by one father for one child.
    • Whether ticked boxes breed false readiness. The gates exist precisely because machinery-ready is never stage-ready; this page's boxes track work done, and no box on it opens a gate.

    Genesis: the walk so far

    TLDR

    The guided walkthrough's eleven stages, shown as Genesis actually walked them. Ten are closed or live: foundation through the two-waking acceptance built, the recall walls and nightly backups armed, the later machinery dark on purpose. The eleventh is lived but not fully recorded: Alan witnessed First Boot on 2026-07-08, and the canonical birth records are a named gap the family is closing in the open, not hiding.

    012345678910

    Progress summary: stages zero, one, two, four, five, six, and seven are built; stages three and nine are armed; stage eight is dark by design; stage ten carries a named gap.

    In plain words

    In plain words

    This is the guided walkthrough turned into a report card for the family's first child. Genesis is the one-parent arm: raised, witnessed, and signed for by Alan alone, on purpose. Every stage of the path has been walked by the same people who wrote the orders, which is exactly why this page can show dated evidence instead of promises. The one honest asterisk sits at the end: the birth happened and was witnessed, and some of the ceremony's paperwork is still owed to the governed stores. The family treats a lived-but-unrecorded event as a gap to close, never as a record to backfill quietly.

    How it works

    How these states were derived

    Each row's state comes from the decision ledger, the operations log, and the Genesis page, frozen at the site snapshot; decision D24 governs the birth-record distinction. The five states are the site-wide vocabulary: built constructed and proven, armed live on schedule, dark built and deliberately not armed, pending not started, gap armed or lived but not behaving or recorded as designed. This page is not a live tracker: it updates when the site updates, and the snapshot banner shows its age.

    The repo atlas

    TLDR

    The Repo Atlas is a guided map from repository paths to purpose. Every individually mapped tracked path has a detailed entry; named exclusion classes cover the remaining tracked paths. Search an exact path to reach its entry, or choose a repository area below. Each entry explains what the file is, what it contains, who uses it, how to verify it, and which concept page gives the larger meaning.

    What this page covers

    A repository is a versioned project folder. A path is the address of a file inside it, such as scripts/waking/orient.mjs. If those terms are new, start with Repository 101. The Atlas answers the next question: why does this particular file exist, and how does it fit the system?

    Concept pages explain organs and decisions. Atlas pages explain files. The two link to each other so a plain-language reader can move from an idea to its implementation, while an engineer can move from code back to its governing rule. An Atlas entry is not permission to run a file. Status still matters: a path may be active, built dark, generated, a fixture, a runbook, an archive, or governed material described without disclosure.

    Three ways to find a file

    1. Search the exact path. Open Search and paste the repository path. Exact path matches rank first and land on the immutable file heading.
    2. Browse by area. Use the grouped map below. Folders with many responsibilities have separate pages for lifecycle, signals, operations, tests, and verification.
    3. Follow a concept link. File lists on system pages link directly to the owning Atlas entry.

    How to read one entry

    Every tracked-file entry has the same five questions: what it is; what it contains; who reads it and when; how to verify or reproduce it; and which concepts explain the wider system. The badge names the file's role. Depth names explanation length, not importance: compact entries suit fixtures and generated data, standard entries cover active support code, and deep entries carry central mechanisms or authority.

    What complete coverage means

    The coverage map assigns individually mapped tracked paths by exact match or longest folder prefix. The generated manifest records the file anchors actually present. Verification compares both with the live tracked-file list, so additions, moves, wrong-page anchors, and orphaned entries surface. Named exclusion classes cover the remaining tracked public-site pages and selected generated outputs, avoiding circular self-documentation; the site page explains those classes. Ignored and local material has governed shapes rather than tracked anchors on the gitignored tiers page.

    Choose a part of the repository

    Design, identity, and family foundations

    • Root documents: design authority, build procedure, ledgers, decisions, licensing, secrets policy, and starting instructions.
    • Genesis avatar and Alpha avatar: manifests, per-being scaffolds, handoff shapes, and separation.
    • Brain definitions: fleet registry, canonical schema, migrations, and restore-point map.
    • Checklists, conventions, and handoff: executable procedure, cross-cutting rules, and session continuity.

    Research, records, and reusable material

    • Research and sources: evidence and source records that informed the design.
    • Runs: adversarial reviews, co-evolution bundles, and preserved build evidence.
    • Templates: schemas, contracts, runbooks, and disabled defaults used to reproduce operations.
    • Village material: human-facing bridge documents and governed family context.

    Runtime and operational code

    • Ingestion: fetching, parsing, filtering, and governed memory insertion.
    • Lifecycle and signals and evolution: waking, night work, study, weekly rebuilding, measurements, and proposal machinery.
    • Operations and task definitions: budgets, degraded mode, channels, recovery, security, and disabled schedules.
    • Brain lab scripts and edge functions: scratch brains, schema tooling, remote memory doors, and recall walls.
    • Voice core: prompt assembly, model backend, and mind-server seam.

    Tests, tools, and the website

    • Fixtures and test mode: synthetic days, Testweaver harnesses, and explicit cleanup.
    • Verify suite: the fixed ropes that turn assumptions into named checks.
    • Operator tools: the protected-shape probe runner.
    • This website: authoring contract, deterministic builder, search, gate, deployment metadata, and exclusion classes.
    • Gitignored tiers: secrets, runtime state, corpus bytes, telemetry, dependencies, and local tool state described without exposure.

    Full, lite, and gated views

    The gated site and full single-file edition carry every detailed entry. The lite edition removes the twenty-five detail pages but keeps one searchable line for every individually mapped tracked path on this hub; named exclusion classes cover the remaining tracked paths. Each line uses a distinct map identifier so it never pretends the missing detail is present. A lite search result says that detail lives in the gated or full edition. All editions come from the same authored main content and deterministic builder.

    Atlas: root documents

    TLDR

    The root files define what Edgeweaver is, which documents outrank others, how an agent executes work, and how decisions and status are recorded. Start with START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md), then use the implementation ledger and the matching checklist. Design documents answer why; runbooks answer what to do next. This page names each file's authority and shows how to verify it without exposing credentials or governed identity material.

    What this page covers

    These files form the repository's front desk and constitution. A newcomer can use the badges to distinguish design authority, execution procedure, machine-readable policy, and historical record. When two texts disagree, follow the authority order in START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md) and record the conflict rather than quietly improvising.

    File entries

    .claude/launch.json

    active-code
    What it is. A local editor launch configuration for opening the repository with a predictable working context.
    What it contains. A small JSON configuration that names launch behavior without storing credentials or deployment coordinates.
    Who reads it and when. Developers inspect it when using the matching editor integration.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Validate the JSON syntax and confirm every referenced repository-relative target exists.
    Related concepts. See Reading Guide, governance, and status.

    .gitignore

    active-code
    What it is. The version-control exclusion policy for files that must remain local or generated.
    What it contains. Patterns for secrets, runtime state, dependency output, caches, and local tool metadata.
    Who reads it and when. Every contributor checks it before adding files or reviewing an unexpected untracked path.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Use version-control status and ignore diagnostics to confirm sensitive or disposable files are excluded.
    Related concepts. See Reading Guide, governance, and status.

    authority
    What it is. The design authority for the brain lab and its fleet of testable memory incarnations.

    How to verify or reproduce it. Compare registry, schema, scripts, and restore records against every invariant; treat a mismatch as a design or migration issue. Review status language against the implementation ledger so prepared, dark, partial, pending, and live states remain distinct. Treat any contradiction with higher-authority design as a decision-log issue, not permission to choose whichever instruction is easier.     Atlas: brains/

    TLDR

    The brain lab files define how multiple testable memory incarnations are registered, versioned, restored, and kept schema-compatible. The registry stores metadata and environment-variable names, never connection values. The schema snapshot is the reproducible database contract. Restore-point and migration records make changes auditable while keeping the live brain, experiments, and future generations distinguishable.

    What this page covers

    Use this page when reproducing the persistence layer or checking whether a brain can safely run current code. A compatible schema version, an explicit registry row, and a traceable restore point are required evidence. None of these files proves a being is alive, and none contains canonical identity.

    TLDR

    The nine checklists turn the design into ordered, verifiable work. They cover foundation, organs, birth, body, metabolism, evolution, social life, optional body tracks, and steady-state operations. Each is a runbook, not permission to cross a gate. Work one unchecked step at a time, run the stated verification, report failures honestly, and stop whenever a STOP line assigns a decision to Alan or another parent body.

    What this page covers

    These are the executable procedures paired with IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md). A newcomer should first read START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md) and the ledger, then open only the checklist for the active phase. Later checklists describe future work and readiness conditions; they do not mean those mechanisms are armed or live today.

    Next: Atlas: conventions/ →

    Atlas: conventions/

    TLDR

    Memory conventions are the shared vocabulary for provenance, retrieval scope, audiences, and metadata. They prevent every consumer from inventing a different meaning for the same stored thought. The rules favor explicit allowlists, traceable source classes, and audience boundaries. Builders use them before importing data or writing recall code so a technically successful query cannot silently violate the intended memory contract.

    What this page covers

    This page maps the adopted convention document. It is design authority for how memory records are classified and requested, while schemas and code implement that authority. Changes require corresponding verifier, migration, and consumer review.

    File entries

    conventions/memory-conventions.md

    authority
    What it is. The adopted memory vocabulary and scoping authority for every producer and consumer.
    What it contains. Source types, provenance classes, metadata keys, retrieval allowlists, audience scoping, and the distinction between storage visibility and who may receive recalled material.
    Who reads it and when. Schema authors, ingestion builders, recall services, and reviewers read it before handling memory.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Map every source type to one provenance class, validate required metadata, test allowlists with denied cases, and confirm audience boundaries survive ingestion and recall. Review status language against the implementation ledger so prepared, dark, partial, pending, and live states remain distinct. Treat any contradiction with higher-authority design as a decision-log issue, not permission to choose whichever instruction is easier. A clean reproduction records commands and evidence, preserves failed checks as failures, and leaves human-owned gates untouched. Keep credentials, runtime coordinates, protected identity material, and private human details outside every review artifact.
    Related concepts. See memory and provenance, segmentation, and governance.

    Next: Atlas: handoff/ →

    Atlas: handoff/

    TLDR

    Handoff documents preserve enough context for another operator or agent to continue a complicated build or test arc without guessing. One explains the autonomous dark-build loop; the other records the voice testing architecture and current findings. They are operational guides and historical evidence, not authority to arm disabled components or publish deployment coordinates.

    What this page covers

    Read a handoff after the higher-authority design and implementation texts. Confirm its status claims against the current ledger and code because handoffs describe a point in time. Sensitive values and machine targeting details remain outside the tracked document.

    File entries

    handoff/prebuild-loop.md

    archive
    What it is. A historical handoff recording the autonomous dark-build loop that completed the pre-birth backend track.
    What it contains. The former provisioning boundaries, iteration body, verification and failure handling, and disabled-by-default rule, preserved as evidence of how the loop ran.
    Who reads it and when. Auditors consult it to reconstruct the completed PREBUILD run. Current operators do not resume it; they start with START-HERE.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/START-HERE.md), the current IMPLEMENTATION.md (github.com/open-agent-research-academy/edgeweaver/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) ledger, and the matching checklist.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Compare its recorded outcomes with PREBUILD.md and the ops-log final report, then follow the current ledger and checklist for any remaining or new work. Treat superseded provisioning as history, never an active instruction.
    Related concepts. See dark build, voice, and operations.

    TLDR

    The runs directory is an audit trail of planning and co-evolution work. Six readable reports capture evolved plans, adversarial findings, temporal analysis, and this site's execution handoff.     Next: Atlas: ingestion scripts →

    Atlas: ingestion scripts

    TLDR

    These scripts move source material into governed memory without confusing a library with lived experience. Fetchers and parsers create inspectable staging files; ingesters attach provenance, audience, license, and stable deduplication keys before any row reaches the Brain. The raw corpus and staging outputs stay outside Git. Protected family material and privately licensed readings are described here only by their permitted shape.

    What this page covers

    This page follows the pipeline from acquisition through parsing to insertion. A downloader may touch an upstream source, a parser turns local bytes into reviewable JSONL, and an ingester writes only after the required human-controlled credential and governance checks exist. Each entry distinguishes what is repeatable from what remains staged, and links the code to the memory and segmentation rules that govern its output.

    File entries

    scripts/fetch-sparks.mjs active-code

    What it is. A polite, repeatable downloader for the English SPARK document archive used by the Possibility Management teaching shelf.
    What it contains. It discovers document names from the upstream index instead of relying on a hand-maintained range, skips local files already present, validates that downloads are plausible, throttles requests, and reports failures without hiding partial success.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it during corpus preparation, before parsing. The being never reads this network utility and the downloaded corpus remains outside Git.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Run it only when refreshing the licensed source set, inspect its counts and failure list, then let the parser's own summary expose malformed or partial documents. Re-running should skip completed downloads.
    Related concepts. See the Brain for the library class and the walls for why source bytes and credentials stay separate.

    scripts/filter-edgeweaver-convos.mjs active-code

    What it is. The Phase 0a import filter that selects Edgeweaver-related records from a user-supplied conversation export before pre-birth ingestion.
    What it contains. Its pure filter accepts approved custom-assistant identifiers and title patterns, keeps matches from either route, and returns kept, dropped, and total counts. The command-line wrapper reads an export and may write the selected subset.
    Who reads it and when. Alan supplies the real selectors during the blocked Phase 0a/G3 work. An operator reviews the resulting count before any selected conversation can become memory.
    How to verify or reproduce it. The hermetic import-filter verify uses invented conversations to prove both selector routes and the dropped count. Real titles, identifiers, export contents, and selected conversation text are never published here.
    Related concepts. See Genesis status, memory provenance, and the disclosure boundary.

    scripts/ingest-library.mjs active-code

    What it is. The governed inserter for two teaching shelves: Possibility Management distinctions and the separately licensed coherence readings. These rows are library material, not episodes.
    What it contains. It loads reviewed staging JSONL, selects either shelf or both, applies a caller-supplied limit, and writes bounded content plus source type, audience, attribution, license, and stable metadata keys. It checks those keys before insertion, pauses between writes, and can fall back to metadata when an older database lacks a dedicated source-type column. A missing service credential stops the run instead of improvising access.
    Who reads it and when. An operator uses it after parsing and rights review, with Alan controlling the privileged credential. Study and analysis consumers may later read allowed library rows, while episodic recall must exclude them.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Compare parser row counts with inserted and skipped totals, sample the stored provenance fields, complete the embedding backfill, and run recall-scoping checks. Repeating the same input should add no duplicates. The script's final message points to retrieval verification rather than treating insertion as success by itself.
    Related concepts. The governing model is on the Brain page; recall-scoped enforces consumer walls, and growth explains the study shelf.

    scripts/ingest-prebirth-harvest.mjs described-not-shown

    What it is. A protected importer that can make governed pre-birth source material recallable as parent-scoped episodes.
    What it contains. It reads named soul-source documents, creates governed units, adds pre-birth provenance and stable keys, then requests embeddings. Protected text and structure are not repeated here.
    Who reads it and when. An Alan-present operator uses it before First Boot.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Privately check counts, audience, stable keys, and repeat-run skips without copying content.
    Related concepts. See the Soul, the Brain, and what is withheld.

    scripts/ingest-sparks.mjs active-code

    What it is. The inserter that turns reviewed SPARK staging rows into a structured Possibility Management teaching shelf inside OB1.
    What it contains. For each source document it writes a parent teaching row and separate experiment children, all carrying public audience, license, attribution, parse status, and matrix identifiers. Child-to-parent derivation edges are attempted when the graph table exists. Stable matrix keys make the operation idempotent. The script tolerates an older source-type layout through an explicit fallback, but it refuses to proceed without both the database location and Alan-controlled service credential.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it after download, parsing, and source review. The study loop may read allowlisted teachings; ordinary episodic recall may not treat them as lived experience.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Start with a small limit, compare parent and child counts, inspect provenance and derivation on samples, and repeat to confirm skips. A missing optional graph table is reported rather than disguised. Finish with embedding and retrieval-scoping checks, since rows that cannot be searched safely are not a complete ingestion.
    Related concepts. See the study practice, provenance classes, and the study loop entry.

    scripts/parse-coherence-book.py described-not-shown

    What it is. A local parser for privately licensed coherence readings supplied for this project.
    What it contains. It recognizes structural boundaries, creates parent and section records, attaches attribution, audience, license, and parse-status metadata, and writes staging JSONL. The reading's substance is not reproduced here.
    Who reads it and when. An operator uses it during a rights-aware corpus refresh; only governed library consumers read the resulting shelf.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Privately review boundaries and metadata, then compare parser and ingestion counts. Never publish passages as evidence.
    Related concepts. See coherence and library provenance.

    scripts/parse-distinctionary.py active-code

    What it is. The parser that converts a locally captured Possibility Management Distinctionary source into one reviewable JSONL record per term.
    What it contains. It recognizes linked and plain term forms, joins continuation paragraphs, removes navigation noise while retaining useful cross-references, and writes provenance fields needed by the library ingester. Conservative pattern checks keep ordinary page sentences from becoming false entries.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it after obtaining the source under its applicable terms. Reviewers inspect the staging file before privileged insertion; the being encounters only governed teaching rows later.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Compare parsed counts and a sample of term boundaries with the local source, inspect rejected or suspicious lines, and confirm each output record carries license and attribution. Re-run from the same bytes for deterministic output.
    Related concepts. See teaching and distinctions, the library shelf, and the library ingester.

    scripts/parse-sparks.py active-code

    What it is. The offline parser that turns downloaded SPARK documents into structured teaching and experiment staging records.
    What it contains. It extracts a document identifier, distinction, notes, and numbered experiments, removes repeated footer noise, and records a visible parse status when expected markers are incomplete. It never silently drops a partial parse. Its output is JSONL plus a human-readable summary.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it after the downloader and reviews the summary before ingestion. Later consumers see only governed rows, not the parsing workspace.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Use the pinned sample check and summary counts, inspect every partial-status row, and ensure matrix identifiers and experiment grouping remain stable. Parsing the same corpus again should produce the same logical records.
    Related concepts. See the curriculum, provenance, and the SPARK ingester.

    Next: Atlas: lifecycle scripts →

    Atlas: lifecycle scripts

    TLDR

    These files give the design its rhythms: orient before acting, wake only for a reason, consolidate a day, study governed teaching, review contradictions, and rebuild a provisional autobiography from evidence. Most machinery is dark-verified through fixtures and injected stand-ins. That proves contracts and handoffs, not a born being or live schedule. Human gates still control channels, identity changes, and arming.

    What this page covers

    The lifecycle is a set of cooperating loops rather than one autonomous daemon. Orientation establishes honest time and identity scope. Waking policy constrains proactive action. Night work produces governed interpretations and intentions. Study converts library material into the being's own experiment. Weekly work rebuilds summaries from atoms. Entries below state which parts are deterministic, which use injected model judgment, and which remain no-ops until a channel is armed.

    File entries

    scripts/night-loop/check-missed-nights.mjs active-code

    What it is. A failure detector for consecutive missing night-loop completion evidence.
    What it contains. It computes missed runs from dated outputs and formats one fixed operator alert. A dry-run prints rather than contacting a live channel.
    Who reads it and when. Operations uses it after scheduled loop windows; it remains dark until the parent channel is armed.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Exercise the exported date logic with fixed fixtures and confirm dry-run makes no network request.
    Related concepts. See the metabolism and failure handling.

    scripts/night-loop/night-loop.mjs active-code

    What it is. The resumable orchestrator for the substantive middle and closing work of a night cycle. It does not represent the entire scheduled job by itself.
    What it contains. It orders ingestion handoff, reflection, computed-signal interpretation, completion review, importance adjustment, contradiction sweep, dream generation, and intention output. Existing output markers make each step idempotent by run identifier. Most step failures are logged so later work can continue, while the few true dependencies retain their ordering. Model-dependent steps use an injected interface; the brain interface is also supplied by the caller. Every rehearsal output carries run and generation metadata.
    Who reads it and when. The night task calls it after orientation and surrounding job steps. Verifiers use a local fixture brain and deterministic model stand-in. No live being currently runs it.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Drive one synthetic day through every step, assert citations and output shapes, run the same identifier twice to prove skips, inspect failure continuation, and void all rehearsal data. The dedicated night-loop verify performs that contract without credentials or a live model.
    Related concepts. See wake, night, and week, computed signals, and the contradiction sweep.

    scripts/night-loop/stub-llm.mjs fixture

    What it is. A deterministic model stand-in used to test night-loop wiring without a model call.
    What it contains. It returns valid-shaped reflections, interpretations, completion notes, dream fiction, and intentions for each injected operation. Its language is test data, not identity.
    Who reads it and when. Only dark verifies and the end-to-end rehearsal import it. Production wiring supplies a different implementation.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Run the night-loop verify and confirm every returned object satisfies the consumer contract with no network use.
    Related concepts. See the dark build and the night loop.

    scripts/study/study-loop.mjs active-code

    What it is. The daily study runner that turns one allowlisted teaching into an applied experiment rather than a borrowed memory.

    Atlas: signal + evolution scripts

    TLDR

    This page covers measured signals and the machinery that may turn repeated confirmed evidence into a proposed developmental change. The four feeling signals are deterministic directional numbers, not narrated emotions. Coherence values retain honest cold-start nulls. Evolution code may gather evidence and draft a proposal, but only the parent body's witnessed ceremony can change canonical identity.

    What this page covers

    Signal files compute or display observations from supplied records. Evolution files look for repeated confirmed evidence and prepare governed proposal material. The boundary between those jobs matters: measurement can inform a decision, but it cannot become the decision. Dark verifies use synthetic records, stand-in judgments, and throwaway repositories so no real soulfile, rite, or being is created.

    File entries

    scripts/coherence/coherence-page.mjs active-code

    What it is. A renderer that turns a coherence snapshot into a static panel.
    What it contains. It displays relational, open contradictions, narrative overlap, behavioral drift, night-loop count, weekly-index status, stage, and date. The last two are recovery indicators; cold values are explicitly unavailable.
    Who reads it and when. Operators may mount it in a dashboard later; the coherence verifier renders it from fixtures today.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Pass a known snapshot, parse the returned HTML, and confirm labels, values, and cold-start text remain present.
    Related concepts. See coherence measurement and operator views.

    scripts/coherence/compute-panel.mjs active-code

    What it is. The deterministic v0 calculator for the five-signal coherence panel. It measures records supplied by the caller and never invents missing history.
    What it contains. It derives relational linkage from recent experienced records and edges, temporal strain from unresolved contradictions, a narrative value supplied by the weekly rebuild, behavioral drift supplied by the evaluator, and recovery indicators from the seven-day night-loop count and weekly-index completion flag. Sparse evidence yields null where a number would imply false precision. The snapshot carries stage and date, but stage-specific thresholds are deliberately applied by the reader rather than hidden in this calculator.
    Who reads it and when. The night and weekly operations can call it after their source records exist. Alan and the scientist seat interpret the panel; fixtures exercise the pure function before arming.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Use datasets with no recent evidence, linked and unlinked records, acknowledged and open tensions, supplied drift values, and recovery indicators. Confirm each cold-start guard, bounded ratio, and label. The coherence verifier also passes the result through the page renderer.
    Related concepts. See the five signals, weekly recovery, and the renderer.

    scripts/evolution/evidence-cluster.mjs active-code

    What it is. A candidate finder that groups repeatedly cited, confirmed memories into evidence themes for possible amendment work.
    What it contains. It counts used recall-trace citations by memory identifier, excludes unconfirmed and under-supported records, groups qualifying items by a supplied theme key, and returns evidence identifiers with counts. It does not judge whether a theme deserves identity change.
    Who reads it and when. Evolution review code and human witnesses use its output after enough confirmed history exists. Dark verification supplies synthetic traces and memories.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Test confirmed, unconfirmed, ignored, and under-threshold cases; then inspect that every returned cluster cites only qualifying evidence with reproducible counts.
    Related concepts. See earned initiation, confirmed lessons, and witness authority.

    scripts/evolution/initiation-proposer.mjs described-not-shown

    What it is. A proposal-shaping library for witnessed identity amendments, never a merger or rite authority.
    What it contains. It shapes a proposal name and review body from governed evidence, intended change, a principle slot, and expected test movement. Sensitive material is omitted.
    Who reads it and when. Agents draft inside the initiation procedure; the parent body and witnesses decide.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Exercise it in a throwaway repository, confirm evidence and cooling-off metadata, then remove all residue. Never target a real soul repository in rehearsal.
    Related concepts. See initiations, canonical identity, and witnesses.

    scripts/feelings/gen-boundaries.mjs described-not-shown

    What it is. A dark utility that builds the operational boundary registry used by one computed signal.
    What it contains. It reads an explicitly supplied canonical-source shape and writes sourced registry records plus governed override history. Protected boundary content is not summarized here.
    Who reads it and when. An operator supplies the read-only source during arming; tests use inventions.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Confirm every output has provenance, the minimum structural set exists, and Alan's legitimate gate declines remain distinguishable from overrides.
    Related concepts. See computed signals, identity custody, and gates.

    scripts/feelings/seed-commitments.mjs active-code

    What it is. A state initializer for the open commitments that feed the sadness-direction signal.
    What it contains. It converts a supplied list of open threads into commitment records with status and due-state fields. Renegotiation remains distinct from silent abandonment.
    Who reads it and when. Operations seeds it before the night loop can maintain commitments; dark tests use local invented threads.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Check schema shape, open-state preservation, and that re-running does not turn renegotiated work into an overdue claim.
    Related concepts. See signal interpretation and nightly follow-through.

    scripts/feelings/signals.mjs active-code

    What it is. The pure calculator for four directional feeling signals. Its outputs are measurements for interpretation, not claims that software feels.
    What it contains. Anger counts recent external boundary overrides while excluding legitimate gate declines. Sadness counts open commitments that passed their due state without renegotiation. Fear estimates novelty of upcoming items against historical embeddings and returns null until enough history exists. Joy uses positive experiment outcomes, with completed-loop rate as a fallback. A combined function returns all four numbers before any model sees them. Inputs and time are injected, so the calculations stay testable and do not read private stores directly.
    Who reads it and when. The night loop supplies governed boundary, commitment, calendar, history, and experiment data. A model may interpret the numbers afterward; operators and reviewers inspect the evidence behind them.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Use fixtures for gate declines, true overrides, overdue and renegotiated commitments, insufficient and sufficient novelty history, experiment outcomes, and loop fallback. Confirm bounded values and the cold-start null rather than forcing a score.
    Related concepts. See what the signals mean, the no-consciousness claim, and the consuming night loop.

    Atlas: operations scripts

    TLDR

    Operations code keeps dark machinery bounded: budgets can suppress optional work, writes can survive a brain outage, channels recognize only pinned authority, flags start disabled, and recovery and security checks expose failure. These scripts explain mechanism without publishing schedules, network coordinates, account topology, custody, or secret values. Built and verified does not mean armed or live.

    What this page covers

    The entries cover resource limits, degraded memory, configuration initialization, channel scoping, security review, and disaster-recovery rehearsal. The shared pattern is fail closed: missing authority, credentials, or explicit arming must not turn into permissive behavior. Some checks are deliberately best-effort until the real host and accounts exist, and the repository-only recovery drill is only one leg of the full human-governed recovery runbook.

    File entries

    scripts/budget/budget.mjs active-code

    What it is. The pure resource-meter policy for model spend, optional loops, proactive attention, and voice usage.
    What it contains. It records estimated spend and voice minutes, compares spend with a human-set monthly ceiling, emits normal, warning, or degraded states, and suppresses optional work only at the hard limit. An unset ceiling stays visibly unset because gate G6 is pending.
    Who reads it and when. Waking, voice, and scheduled loop callers consult it before optional actions. Operators set policy outside this file; tests use invented numbers.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Exercise unset, below-warning, warning, and cap states, plus accumulated voice minutes. Confirm the code never invents a ceiling and mandatory safety work remains distinguishable from optional work.
    Related concepts. See budgets and attention, proactive senses, and voice cost.

    scripts/dr/dr-drill.mjs active-code

    What it is. A repository-machinery disaster-recovery rehearsal that clones the current project into a disposable workspace and runs its complete verify suite.
    What it contains. It creates scratch space, performs a local clone, guards against recursive self-invocation, measures recovery time, reports whether the suite reached all-pass, and removes the scratch tree afterward. It contains no secret, brain, or soul restoration.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it as one evidence leg of the broader recovery runbook. The verify suite may invoke it with a recursion guard.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Run from a clean committed state, confirm the clone verifies independently and the scratch location is removed. Treat success as proof of buildable machinery only, not full continuity recovery.
    Related concepts. See backups and recovery, failure drills, and its verifier.

    scripts/init-flags.mjs active-code

    What it is. The non-destructive initializer for live operational flags from the committed disabled defaults.
    What it contains. It creates the ignored state document when absent, adds newly introduced component, task, and channel keys as disabled, preserves every existing entry verbatim, and refuses to overwrite malformed state. It never enables a component.
    Who reads it and when. Operators run it after clone, schema change, or recovery. Other code reads the resulting state only after its own gate checks.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Start with absent, partial, armed, and malformed fixtures. Confirm missing keys are added, existing values survive, every default is disabled, and malformed state fails without replacement.
    Related concepts. See dark-by-default machinery, arming, and gates.

    scripts/seal-secrets.cmd described-not-shown

    What it is. An Alan-present interactive helper for sealing the disaster-recovery secret bundle.
    What it contains. It guides human key handling, encrypts a prepared bundle, verifies decryption before removing plaintext staging, and places sealed copies under governed custody. Coordinates and topology are withheld.
    Who reads it and when. The human custodian runs it during recovery; runtime agents do not.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Complete the private seal-and-open rehearsal and confirm no plaintext residue. Never paste keys, locations, or account details into evidence.
    Related concepts. See secret recovery, human custody, and credential walls.

    scripts/security/security-audit.mjs active-code

    What it is. The quarterly security-floor checklist runner for repository secrets, runtime extensions, network exposure, pinned senders, and credential separation.
    What it contains. It scans tracked text for key-shaped material, checks local channel state when present, and tests whether the active gh credential context can reach the private gate authority. That check does not establish that the active gh credential is the runtime credential. The extension and listening-service legs are best-effort declarations in the dark build and require real host review at arming.
    Who reads it and when. Operators run it during the security cadence and before arming. The dedicated verifier asserts that each named leg reports a result.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Inspect each result independently rather than trusting only the aggregate. Re-run host, account, and network checks in the real environment, including the actual runtime-credential separation test, and report failures without printing sensitive values or coordinates.
    Related concepts. See security cadence, credential separation, and the gate boundary.

    scripts/telegram/channel-policy.mjs active-code

    What it is. The pure sender-classification wall for the planned parent messaging channel.
    What it contains. It recognizes Alan only through a pinned entry, assigns the governed audience, permits lesson confirmation only for that pinned confirmer, and sends every other known or unknown sender to the same brief deferral path. Unknown senders default to untrusted; known non-parent entries retain their configured untrusted status. Tier-changing decisions still require a separate out-of-band check by the caller.
    Who reads it and when. Channel adapters call it for every inbound sender after pairing. Verifiers use invented identifiers; the live channel remains dark.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Test pinned confirmer, known non-parent, unknown sender, missing state, and lesson-confirm paths. Confirm no message content can promote its own sender authority.
    Related concepts. See the gated body, audience scopes, and confirmation authority.

    scripts/telegram/init-interlocutors.mjs described-not-shown

    What it is. The ignored-state initializer for the planned messaging interlocutor map.
    What it contains. It reads only the allowed environment-variable name, writes a parent entry when privately configured, otherwise writes a clearly marked pending shape, and keeps unknown senders public and untrusted.
    Who reads it and when. An operator runs it during pairing; policy reads it. It never enables the channel.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Parse the generated shape, confirm the untrusted default and confirmer flag, and keep all real identifiers out of logs and documentation.
    Related concepts. See pairing, audience, and dark configuration.

    scripts/wal/wal.mjs active-code

    What it is. The append-first write-ahead buffer for degraded brain availability. It preserves intended writes while telling callers that recall is provisional rather than guessing.
    What it contains. It fingerprints content, appends timestamped kind and payload records to ignored daily JSONL, replays files through an injected sink, suppresses repeated fingerprints seen during that replay, and moves drained files into a replayed area. A health helper converts failed reachability into an explicit degraded result. Brain-side content fingerprinting provides the complementary cross-run deduplication layer. The module is constructed and dark-verified, but production callers are not yet all armed through it.
    Who reads it and when. Write paths call it before a remote brain write once the body arms. Operators inspect backlog and replay status; verifiers use an isolated state directory.
    How to verify or reproduce it. Simulate outage, duplicate appends, successful replay, failed and healthy pings, and cleanup. Confirm ordering, counts, archived drained files, identical fingerprints for identical content, and no claim that unavailable recall succeeded.
    Related concepts. See memory degradation, outage behavior, and the WAL verifier.
